stem:
Avni writes the numbers $14 \times 6$ and $14 \times 9$. She wants their highest common factor.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call the answer the common multiplier $14$, and stop with HCF $= 14$.
Say HCF $= 14$ even when the remaining factors $6$ and $9$ still share a common factor.
HCF $= 14 \times \mathrm{HCF}(6, 9) = 14 \times 3 = 42$, because $14$ joins any leftover shared factor.
Choose $14$ only because $14$ is the largest printed number among $14$, $6$, and $9$.

teacher.key_rationale: A shared multiplier enters the HCF, and shared factors in the remaining multipliers can remain: HCF(14×6,14×9)=14×3=42. Stopping at 14 alone substitutes the visible multiplier for the full HCF. Ignoring leftover shared factors omits a needed check. Grabbing the largest print is surface capture.
